scope: Standing Adelaide Gaol, including the Georgian front range and arched double door, outer and inner walls, two historic masonry towers, the radial cell blocks and prison yards.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: History Trust records the radial plan, the original red brick and stone with imported sandstone for coping, sills and towers, the 1862 bluestone range and 1864 two-storey additions, and the 1972 central watch tower.
The gaol operator documents the 1841 opening, incomplete original plans and major 1879 addition.
The gaol identifies the 1841 administration building and sally port, circle, guard tower, remand centre, original cell block, new building and other visitor locations.
The conservation architects describe stone remediation and slate reroofing of parts of the site.

The City of Adelaide records roughly 18-foot limestone outer walls, 10-foot brick yard partitions, two octagonal masonry towers (one built without its castellations), and the two-storey 1879 T-shaped cell block.
